_spec.law: Facts resolve to the original verified claim record. A layout rebuild does not reverify reporting.

dek.text: The UT System's health care AI laboratory funded twelve pilots for its hospitals and medical schools. Only the no-show entry at UTHealth Houston states what it already saved.

introduction.text: [The University of Texas System has a laboratory for health care AI, UT REAL Health AI](c1), [launched in 2025 on legislative approval and dedicated funding](c2). [It announced funding for {{number:c6}} pilot projects to advance the use of AI in health care across the UT System](c6). [They were chosen from {{number:c7}} systemwide submissions](c7), and [the awards total more than {{money:c8}}](c8).
[The laboratory's page carries no announcement date](c6), so the pilots can be placed only by the day the page was read. One of its entries states a result.

sections.heading: What the twelve pilots put into hospitals

paragraphs.text: [At UT San Antonio, a pilot deploys an AI clinical assistant called Leah, trained on more than {{number:c47}} trauma cases, across seven UT hospital sites for emergency triage and transfer decisions](c47). [At UT Austin, a smartphone app listens for fetal movement to help prevent stillbirth](c11), and [the page gives its accuracy as {{number:c48}} percent](c48).

[At UTMB Galveston, a pilot deploys AI referral triage](c13). [The tool reads the health record, assigns an urgency score and routes patients to a level of care](c49). [At UT Dell Medical School, a pilot on patient engagement](c15) [implements six AI tools built into Epic, among them tools that automate lab result messaging and generate patient-facing imaging summaries](c51).

[Another Dell Medical School pilot will use large language models on free-text clinical notes across more than {{number:c17}} million patient records to improve suicide risk detection](c17). [At UTHealth Houston, a pilot called Priorities AI asks older adults about their surgical goals before they meet their surgeon](c50). [A wrong-tooth pilot pairs computer vision on dental images with language processing of surgical notes](c52). [A pilot led from UT Tyler uses AI to widen access to retinal screening](c21).

Two expand platforms that already ran elsewhere. [A trial prescreening platform was validated on nearly {{number:c19}} patients at UT Southwestern](c19). [An AI grading platform for medical school simulation exams has run for more than three years and supported more than {{number:c20}} encounters](c20).

sections.heading: The one count on the page

paragraphs.text: [One funded project expands AI-powered no-show reduction across UT System health institutions](c16). [The page credits it with saving more than {{number:c22}} appointments and {{money:c22}} in revenue at UTHealth Houston](c22). The page cites no measurement or audit behind that figure.

[The project is set to expand to UT Health San Antonio, where the page projects it will recover at least {{number:c23}} appointments a year](c23). The San Antonio figure is a projection and the Houston figure is a report, and the two are not the same kind of number.

sections.heading: What the page does not establish

paragraphs.text: [Of the {{number:c6}} funded projects](c6), [only the no-show entry states what it already saved](c22). The other entries describe the work a tool does or will do, or how widely an earlier platform has run, rather than a count of what it saved.

[The page does not say when the awards were made](c6), and it does not say how any pilot will be measured or when results will be published. A reader can't tell from it which hospitals already use a given tool and which are still preparing to.

[The laboratory's 2026 symposium is set for October 7th and 8th in Austin](c24). [Its page names the laboratory's executive director, Dr. Nyma Shah of UT MD Anderson Cancer Center](c3), [and its chair, Dr. Peter McCaffrey of UTMB](c4). [The laboratory's page carries a link to register for the symposium](c54).
